messages:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up: we need a clear pattern for exposing deploy-scoped controls (routing, eviction, telemetry). Options: keep tenant-only, a separate deployment API, or a single endpoint with explicit scope. Short takes?

sam: single endpoint with explicit scope seems tidy: PATCH /v1/config with {scope: "tenant"|"deployment", deploy_id: ...}. Forces explicit intent.

li: agree on explicitness but we must gate deployment scope. Hosted customers shouldn't be able to change deploy-scoped settings unless enrolled. RBAC + audit required.

anya: Implementation constraints: runtime needs deploy_id on hot path for batching/cache key decisions. We can't parse query params deep in hot code. Router should normalize ctx.scope + ctx.deploy_id early.

sam: caching note: include deploy_id in batching key only when scope==deployment or when deploy-level overrides exist to avoid key explosion.

li: telemetry: add trace tags: scope and policy_source (deploy_override|tenant|system). Emit override_applied boolean. Makes postmortems easier.

ops-bot: ops-bot: test hint - header x-scope + x-deploy-id shows up in traces as span.tags.scope/span.tags.deploy.id

anya: UX: for hosted, require Console confirmation for sensitive ops. API returns 409 "confirm via console" when advanced write attempted without console confirmation. Dedicated/Private can use API if role permitted.

sam: rollout: 1) RFC + docs; 2) console opt-in; 3) router normalization + trace tags; 4) runtime batching toggle behind flag; 5) Dedicated canary.

li: action items: sam - draft router normalization PR; anya - spec console confirmation flow; I'll document cache key rule and perf estimate. We'll reconvene after RFC draft.
